source.title: Hierarchical Prototype Emergence in Modern Hopfield Models

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplemental material supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Tests prototype reconstruction as generalization in a dense associative memory, including an analytical hierarchy model and a Fashion-MNIST experiment; this setting differs from the versions' standard supervised learning and held-out generalization.
record.gate_note: Reports energy-gap stability of stored leaves and unseen ancestor prototypes in a hierarchical memory model, plus Fashion-MNIST reconstruction outcomes. These bear on generalization broadly, but do not test the listed versions about natural-label held-out test error, architecture/optimizer/batch/regularization comparisons, sharpness measures, or influence-based example removal. Figure 4 reports phase regions and representative images without numerical Hamming distances in the text; no separate numeric row is reconstructed from the figure.
record.test_reason: The study measures stored-pattern recall and unseen-prototype reconstruction in dense Hopfield memories. These are different constructs from every listed version. It reports no supervised held-out classification comparisons, random-label experiment, or magnitude-aware weight-sharpness analysis. Its own prototype results therefore do not test V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: hierarchical correlations can produce unstored ancestor prototypes as stable minima in dense Hopfield networks, with reconstruction level controlled by memory count and activation degree. Fashion-MNIST provides qualitative analogous behavior. These conclusions concern prototype reconstruction rather than the supervised generalization effects in V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: Uses polynomial-activation dense Hopfield energy descent on hierarchically correlated binary memories; generalization is defined as local stability/prototype reconstruction, not standard supervised training with held-out natural-label test error.
record.method_sensitivity: The stability and recovered hierarchy level vary with branching factor K and activation sharpness n; the analytical large-K plateau also varies with prototype depth ℓ. Fashion-MNIST outcomes are shown across sharpness and samples per group.

fits_no_version.finding: Unstored ancestor prototypes can become stable local minima; suitably scaling branching factor and activation degree makes a given prototype's instability probability vanish.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dense Hopfield memories can reconstruct latent hierarchical prototypes under suitable correlation, sample-size, and activation-degree conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing the number of correlated memories affects hierarchy levels differently: leaf stability deteriorates at fixed activation degree, intermediate prototypes have an optimal regime, and root stability improves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Associative-memory recall and prototype stability depend on which hierarchy level is probed and how memory count scales with activation degree.

fits_no_version.finding: Fashion-MNIST ankle-boot queries reach the original image, boot prototype, shoe prototype, or blank root as activation degree and images per class vary.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dense associative memories built from binarized Fashion-MNIST exhibit parameter-dependent transitions between exemplar recall and emergent prototype reconstruction.

record.problems: The real-data experiment is qualitative and reports no numerical Hamming distances in the supplied text. The analytic model assumes a homogeneous tree, uniform correlation/noise, and a single-layer network; the authors note that more complex datasets with spatial symmetries produced washed-out and blurry emergent memories in their numerical experiments, without giving measurements.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 4 colors the phase diagram by Hamming distance but the supplied text gives no recoverable numeric values; no figure-only row was reconstructed. No additional numeric or distinct condition-specific Fashion-MNIST outcomes are stated in prose.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy using the same architectures and training recipes.
Network-width sweeps beyond zero training error and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classification performance and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance, training–test gaps, and comparison with other generalization measures. Activation sharpness n is a different quantity.
Influence-based memorization estimates and test accuracy after targeted versus random example removal.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T3 classification should be T6 because a new setting qualifies as a test only when its results measure a listed claim. The cannot_determine row states refer to V1–V8, not to whether the paper establishes its own prototype results. No additional result bearing on those versions requires a missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out natural-label generalization.
Width sweep and test error beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the training-test gap.
Removal of influential memorized examples and resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: Dense Hopfield network with hierarchical memories (analytical model)
rows.operation_detail: Analytically evaluate squared coefficient of variation of the energy gap for unseen ancestor prototypes across K and activation degree n.

conditions.value: q −2 ≪ K ≪ q −(2n−1) for decreasing regime

rows.measure: Squared coefficient of variation (Cℓv)2 of energy gap; proxy for probability an ancestor prototype is unstable.
rows.value: (C0<ℓ<hv)2 decreases roughly as ∼ K −1 until a minimum point; with n tuned to n∗(K), minimum (Cℓv)2 decreases as roughly ∝ K −1.
rows.locator: Main text, Memory Stability and Emergent Minima; Fig. 2; Supplemental Material S2.B, Theorem 6
rows.note: The analysis asserts that the probability for an ancestor prototype to be unstable decreases with K, and can be driven toward zero when n is increased commensurately. This is a stability/generalization proxy in the toy associative-memory model, not held-out test error.
rows.check: Valid out-of-scope analytical result. Energy-gap variation measures prototype stability, not any listed version's effect. The supplement establishes bounds on variation and instability probability; variation is not itself the instability probability.

source_check.locator_found: Memory Stability and Emergent Minima, pp. 3–4; Fig. 2; Supplement S2.B.1, Eqs. S38–S39.

rows.subject: Dense Hopfield network with hierarchical memories (analytical model)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate squared coefficient of variation for ancestor prototype stability in the large-K limit.

conditions.value: K → ∞ at fixed n, h, q

rows.measure: Squared coefficient of variation (Cℓv)2 of energy gap.
rows.value: (C0<ℓ<hv)2 → q −2ℓ − 1 as K → ∞; plateau diverges rapidly with ℓ.
rows.locator: Main text, Memory Stability and Emergent Minima; Supplemental Material S2.B, Prototype Reconstruction
rows.note: The authors say adding data alone does not improve recall unless model capacity n is increased commensurately; the large-K limit therefore qualifies the decreasing-K regime in R1.
rows.check: The fixed-capacity large-K plateau concerns prototype stability. It is not partial evidence for any listed version; K changes the number of correlated memories, not network width.

source_check.locator_found: Memory Stability and Emergent Minima, p. 3; Supplement S2.B.1, Eq. S37.

rows.subject: Dense Hopfield network with hierarchical memories (analytical model)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate squared coefficient of variation for stored leaf-memory stability as K varies.
rows.measure: Squared coefficient of variation (Cℓ=h v)2 of energy gap.
rows.locator: Main text, Memory Stability and Emergent Minima; Supplemental Material S2.B, Memorization: ℓ = h
rows.note: The paper distinguishes leaf recall from ancestor-prototype generalization; this finding concerns stored-pattern stability.
rows.check: Stored-leaf stability is associative recall, without random-label fitting or held-out natural-label accuracy. The stated large-K limit matches Eq. S40.

source_check.locator_found: Supplement S2.B.2, Eq. S40; main-text discussion of leaf stability, p. 4.

rows.subject: Dense Hopfield network with hierarchical memories (analytical model)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate squared coefficient of variation for root prototype stability as K varies.

conditions.value: Kq2 > 1 for convergence at large h

rows.measure: Squared coefficient of variation (Cℓ=0 v)2 of energy gap.
rows.value: In the large K limit this expression vanishes; at fixed n, h, q the root is the only absolutely stable memory.
rows.locator: Main text, Memory Stability and Emergent Minima; Supplemental Material S2.B, Root Prototype: ℓ = 0
rows.note: A distinct hierarchy-level stability result, not a training-test gap measurement.
rows.check: Root-prototype stability does not measure any listed effect. Its vanishing variation at large K is conditional on the analytical approximation regime.

source_check.locator_found: Supplement S2.B.3, Eqs. S42–S43 and following paragraph.

rows.subject: Dense associative memory on Fashion-MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Binarize images by per-pixel dithering, store them as memories, initialize dynamics at an ankle boot query, and descend energy to a fixed point while sweeping sharpness and images per class.

conditions.value: potential sharpness n and samples per group K

rows.measure: Hamming distance between query and recovered fixed point; text describes fixed-point identity by hierarchy level.
rows.value: Four regimes: query leaf, emergent boot prototype, emergent shoe prototype, and blank root prototype; large n or small K pins the query to the leaf; decreasing n transitions through boot and shoe prototypes, then the root at smallest n.
rows.locator: Main text, Experiment on Fashion-MNIST; Fig. 4
rows.note: The textual result names regimes but supplies no numerical Hamming distances. The paper says the boot and shoe prototypes are not stored explicitly.
rows.check: Fixed-point identity and query-to-reconstruction Hamming distance do not measure held-out classification performance. Correct the claim that no numerical distance is supplied: Figure 4's caption explicitly gives zero distance for the red-circle leaf reconstruction.

source_check.correct: Figure 4 explicitly gives Hamming distance 0 for the red-circle fixed point corresponding to the original query image. Numerical distances for the other regimes are not stated.
source_check.locator_found: Experiment on Fashion-MNIST, pp. 4–5; Fig. 4 caption.
source_check.problem: The reported four regimes are correct, but the row note incorrectly says the text supplies no numerical Hamming distances.

rows.subject: Dense associative memory on Fashion-MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Observe recovered fixed point near the lower triple point of the sharpness/group-size phase diagram.
rows.measure: Qualitative prototype features of the recovered fixed point.
rows.value: The recovered shoe prototype takes on some features of the boot prototype, such as a lift at the front, while remaining largely consistent with the shoe prototype.
rows.locator: Main text, Experiment on Fashion-MNIST; Fig. 4
rows.note: Qualitative transition-region result; no numeric distance is given.
rows.check: The mixed visual features near a phase boundary are a qualitative prototype result, not an incomplete manifestation of any listed version.
